facts.statement: Ningchengopterus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Ningchengopterus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous period (Aptian stage).

facts.statement: This pterosaur genus lived in China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Ningchengopterus es un género de pterosaurios pterodactiloideos que vivió en el Cretácico Inferior de China

facts.statement: Ningchengopterus existed between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Ningchengopterus were discovered in the Yixian Formation in present-day China.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains were found in the Yixian Formation of what is now China.

facts.statement: Ningchengopterus was the first small, toothed pterodactyloid pterosaur fossil discovered in China.
facts.quote: It was the first small toothed pterodactyloid pterosaur specimen found in China.

facts.statement: The species Ningchengopterus liuae was formally named and described by Lü Junchang in 2009.
facts.quote: The type species Ningchengopterus liuae was named and described by Lü Junchang in 2009.

facts.statement: The only known specimen is a juvenile holotype (CYGB-0035) featuring an almost complete articulated skeleton with preserved soft tissues like the flight membrane and pycnofibres.
facts.quote: It is known from a juvenile specimen, holotype CYGB-0035, an almost complete articulated skeleton of a hatchling also showing soft parts, such as the flight membrane and pycnofibres, compressed on a plate and counterplate.

facts.statement: Ningchengopterus possessed approximately fifty teeth, with twelve in the upper jaw and thirteen in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Ningchengopterus was typified by the possession of about fifty teeth, twelve in each upper jaw and thirteen in each lower jaw.

facts.statement: The teeth of Ningchengopterus were curved, conical, and pointed.
facts.quote: The teeth are curved, conical and pointed.

facts.statement: The skull of Ningchengopterus measured thirty-eight millimetres in length.
facts.quote: The skull has a length of thirty-eight millimetres.

facts.statement: Ningchengopterus had an elongated and tapering snout.
facts.quote: The snout is elongated and tapering.

facts.statement: The lower jaws of Ningchengopterus displayed an incipient crest.
facts.quote: The lower jaws show an incipient crest.

facts.statement: Ningchengopterus is classified only as broadly belonging to the Pterodactyloidea superfamily.
facts.quote: The specimen could not be more precisely determined than Pterodactyloidea.

facts.statement: Although Ningchengopterus shared flight finger proportions with Ctenochasmatids like Eosipterus, it lacked other defining traits, so researchers did not place it in that group.
facts.quote: It shared the relative proportions of the first and second phalanx of the flight finger with the Ctenochasmatidae, and especially Eosipterus found in the same formation, but showed no further synapomorphies of that group, so that Lü abstained from placing it in that clade.

facts.statement: The shape of its teeth suggests that Ningchengopterus was a fish eater.
facts.quote: The teeth suggested that Ningchengopterus was a fish eater.

facts.statement: The presence of a fully formed flight membrane in the hatchling supports the hypothesis that pterosaurs provided little parental care and their young could fly shortly after hatching.
facts.quote: The fully formed flight membrane was seen as confirmation of a hypothesis by Mark Unwin that pterosaurs displayed little parental care, their "babies" being able to fly shortly after hatching.

facts.statement: Ningchengopterus belongs to the suborder Pterodactyloidea.
The genus Ningchengopterus was established by Lü J. in 2009.

rejected.statement: The specific name 'liuae' honors Ms Liu Jingyi, who collected the fossil and donated it to science.
rejected.quote: The specific name honours Ms Liu Jingyi who collected the fossil and donated it to science.
